useCase: Clearing mental RAM at the end of the day.
promptText: Here is a messy brain-dump of everything on my mind right now (ideas, anxieties, tasks, random thoughts): [Paste Brain Dump]. Act as my personal assistant. Sort this into actionable tasks, ideas to save for later, and things I just need to let go of. Format it cleanly.
proTip: Do this 30 minutes before bed to drastically improve your sleep quality by getting open loops out of your head.

title: The Keyword Cluster Map
useCase: Building topical authority for a new website or blog.
promptText: Act as an expert SEO strategist. My website is in the [Niche/Industry] niche. The primary topic I want to rank for is [Core Topic]. Create a 'Topic Cluster' strategy with 1 Pillar Page title and 10 related Sub-Cluster blog post titles. For each sub-cluster, provide the primary long-tail keyword.
proTip: Internal linking is crucial. Always link your sub-cluster articles back to the main pillar page to boost its authority.

title: The Meta Tag Optimizer
useCase: Writing high-CTR title tags and meta descriptions.
promptText: I am publishing a webpage about [Page Topic]. The primary keyword I want to rank for is [Primary Keyword]. Generate 5 SEO-optimized Title Tags (under 60 characters) and 5 Meta Descriptions (under 155 characters). Make them highly clickable and include a strong call-to-action.
proTip: Include numbers, brackets [ ], or action verbs in your title tags to significantly increase organic Click-Through Rate (CTR).

title: The 30-Day Content Calendar
useCase: Planning a month of social media content in 5 minutes.
promptText: Create a 30-day social media content calendar for a [Business Type/Niche]. The target audience is [Target Audience]. The main goal is [Marketing Goal, e.g., brand awareness, lead generation]. Format it as a table with columns: Day, Content Theme (e.g., Educational, Entertaining, Promotional), Post Format (e.g., Reel, Carousel), and a brief Post Idea.
proTip: Follow the 80/20 rule: 80% of your calendar should provide free value, and only 20% should directly promote your product.

title: The PAS Ad Copywriter
useCase: Drafting high-converting Facebook or Instagram Ads.
promptText: Write ad copy for Facebook/Instagram promoting my [Product/Service]. Use the Problem-Agitate-Solve (PAS) copywriting framework. The target audience struggles with [Customer Pain Point]. The primary benefit of my product is [Main Benefit]. Keep the tone [Tone, e.g., empathetic, urgent].
proTip: Ask the AI to generate 3 different 'Hooks' (the first sentence) for this ad so you can A/B test which one grabs the most attention.

title: The Backlink Outreach Pitch
useCase: Sending cold emails to secure high-quality SEO backlinks.
promptText: Write a cold outreach email to [Target Role, e.g., a blog editor, marketing manager] at [Target Website Name]. I want to ask them to add a backlink to my highly-researched article about [My Article Topic]. Mention that I noticed a broken link or an outdated stat in their article about [Their Article Topic]. Keep it short, personalized, and non-spammy.
proTip: Never ask for a link in the very first sentence. Add value first by pointing out a typo or sharing their post on your socials.

title: The YouTube SEO Master
useCase: Optimizing video metadata for the YouTube search algorithm.
promptText: I am uploading a YouTube video about [Video Topic]. The main target keyword is [Primary Keyword]. Generate an SEO-optimized video title (high clickability), a 3-paragraph video description (including timestamps), and a comma-separated list of 15 highly relevant tags.
proTip: Put your most important keywords in the first 2 sentences of the description, as this is what YouTube reads most heavily.

title: The Competitor Gap Finder
useCase: Outranking a competitor by writing a more comprehensive article.
promptText: My competitor is currently ranking #1 on Google for the keyword '[Target Keyword]'. Their article covers these main points: [List Competitor's Main Headers]. Act as an SEO expert and tell me what 'content gaps' they missed. Give me 5 unique angles or sections I can add to my article to make it 10x better than theirs.
proTip: Google rewards 'Information Gain'. If you just rewrite the competitor's post, you won't outrank them. You must add net-new information.

title: The Welcome Email Sequence
useCase: Nurturing new leads automatically via email.
promptText: A user just joined my email list by downloading my free lead magnet: [Lead Magnet Topic]. Write a 3-part automated 'Welcome Sequence' email campaign. Email 1: Deliver the magnet & introduce myself. Email 2: Share a valuable related tip/story. Email 3: Soft pitch my paid product: [Paid Product Name].
proTip: Space these emails out (e.g., Day 1, Day 2, Day 4). Build trust before asking for the sale in Email 3.

title: The Local SEO Booster
useCase: Optimizing a Google Business Profile for local search.
promptText: I own a local [Business Type, e.g., Plumber, Coffee Shop] located in [City, Neighborhood]. Write a 400-word 'From the Business' description for my Google Business Profile. Naturally weave in these local SEO keywords: [List 3-4 Local Keywords]. Highlight that we offer [Key Service/Differentiator].
proTip: Consistency is key in Local SEO. Ensure your NAP (Name, Address, Phone number) in this profile matches exactly what is on your website.

title: The Buyer Persona Builder
useCase: Creating a hyper-specific target avatar for better targeting.
promptText: Build a detailed buyer persona for a company selling [Product/Service]. Include their age, occupation, income level, and geographic location. More importantly, list their top 3 psychological pain points, their ultimate desired transformation, and the top 3 objections they have to buying.
proTip: Give your persona a name (e.g., 'Marketing Mary'). It makes it much easier to write copy when you imagine writing to one specific person.

title: The Viral Short-Form Hook
useCase: Stopping the scroll on TikTok, Instagram Reels, or YouTube Shorts.
promptText: I am recording a short-form video about [Video Topic]. The goal is to get views and saves. Generate 10 controversial, curiosity-driven, or highly relatable 'Hooks' (the first 3 seconds of the video script). Do not use generic greetings. Get straight to the point.
proTip: The best hooks challenge a common belief. (e.g., 'Stop doing X. Do Y instead.')

title: The E-Commerce SEO Describer
useCase: Writing product descriptions that rank and convert.
promptText: Write an SEO-optimized product description for an e-commerce store. The product is [Product Name]. The primary keyword is [Target Keyword]. Include a 50-word engaging opening paragraph, a bulleted list of 5 technical features, and a short FAQ section answering 2 common customer questions.
proTip: Never use the manufacturer's default description. Google penalizes duplicate content. Always generate your own unique copy.

title: The Semantic Keyword (LSI) Finder
useCase: Finding related keywords to sprinkle into your articles naturally.
promptText: I am writing a comprehensive SEO article about '[Main Keyword]'. Give me a list of 20 LSI (Latent Semantic Indexing) keywords and related entities that Google would expect to see in an expert-level article on this topic. Group them logically by sub-topic.
proTip: Don't keyword stuff. Use these terms naturally as H2 headers or as bullet points within your content.

title: The Review Generator
useCase: Asking past clients for testimonials without being awkward.
promptText: Write a short, polite email to a past client who recently purchased my [Service/Product]. Ask them if they would be willing to leave a Google/Trustpilot review. Provide them with a 3-question 'template' they can use to easily write the review if they don't know what to say.
proTip: Reducing friction gets you more reviews. The template questions should be: What was the problem? What was the result? Would you recommend us?

title: The Podcast Guest Pitch
useCase: Getting booked on podcasts for digital PR and backlinks.
promptText: Write a pitch email to the host of the [Podcast Name] podcast. My expertise is in [My Expertise/Niche]. Pitch 3 specific, unique conversation topics or controversial takes I could discuss on their show that would bring massive value to their audience. Keep the tone respectful but confident.
proTip: Podcast hosts ignore generic pitches. Mention a specific detail from a recent episode of theirs in the first paragraph to prove you actually listen.

title: The A/B Test Ideator
useCase: Brainstorming new angles to test when ad performance drops.
promptText: My current digital ads for [Product/Service] are experiencing ad fatigue. Give me 5 completely distinct A/B testing angles I can try. (e.g., Use an Urgency angle, a Social Proof angle, an 'Us vs. Them' angle). Describe the visual creative and the primary text copy for each angle.
proTip: Only test one variable at a time (e.g., change the image but keep the text the same) so you know exactly what caused the performance shift.

title: The Tagline Brainstorm
useCase: Creating a memorable slogan for a brand or product.
promptText: Brainstorm 10 catchy, memorable taglines for a company called [Company Name]. The company does [Describe Company Function]. The target audience is [Target Audience]. Provide a mix of short/punchy taglines, descriptive taglines, and emotional taglines.
proTip: The best taglines are usually under 5 words. (Think Nike: 'Just Do It', or Apple: 'Think Different').

title: The Freelance Writer Brief
useCase: Delegating content creation with crystal-clear SEO instructions.
promptText: Create a comprehensive SEO content brief to send to a freelance writer. The topic is [Article Topic] and the target keyword is [Keyword]. Outline the desired word count, the required H2s and H3s, the target audience, the desired tone of voice, and exactly what the Call to Action should be at the end.
proTip: A good brief prevents endless revisions. Tell the writer exactly what NOT to include as well.

title: The Influencer Collab DM
useCase: Reaching out to creators for UGC or sponsored posts.
promptText: Write a direct message (DM) to an Instagram/TikTok influencer in the [Niche] space. I want to send them a free sample of my [Product] in exchange for a dedicated post or an unboxing video. Make the message sound casual, complimentary of their recent content, and mutually beneficial.
proTip: Micro-influencers (10k-50k followers) usually have higher engagement rates and are more willing to do product-exchange deals than massive accounts.

title: The Product Launch Timeline
useCase: Structuring a multi-channel marketing campaign.
promptText: I am launching a new [Product/Feature] in exactly 14 days. Create a day-by-day marketing launch strategy. Tell me exactly what I should be posting, emailing, or doing each day leading up to the launch (The Tease phase), on Launch Day, and post-launch (The Follow-up phase).
proTip: Don't stop marketing on Launch Day. The 3 days *after* launch usually generate the most sales if you use urgency (e.g., 'Discount ends tonight!').

title: The YC Investor Grill
useCase: Preparing for brutal, rapid-fire investor pitch meetings.
promptText: Act as a ruthless Y-Combinator partner. My startup is called [Startup Name] and we are building [What You Are Building] for [Target Audience]. Ask me 5 extremely difficult, skeptical questions about my market size, defensibility, and team. Wait for my response before giving me harsh but constructive feedback.
proTip: Don't use marketing jargon in your answers. Investors want clear, concise, and numbers-driven responses.

title: The Lean Canvas Generator
useCase: Mapping out a 1-page business plan for a new idea.
promptText: I have an idea for a startup that does [Startup Idea]. Generate a complete Lean Canvas for this idea. Fill out the following 9 sections: Problem, Solution, Key Metrics, Unique Value Proposition, Unfair Advantage, Channels, Customer Segments, Cost Structure, and Revenue Streams.
proTip: Focus heavily on the 'Unfair Advantage'. If your only advantage is 'we work harder', investors won't bite.

title: The Competitor Matrix
useCase: Analyzing the market to find gaps you can exploit.
promptText: My startup is entering the [Industry/Niche] space. My top 3 competitors are [Competitor 1], [Competitor 2], and [Competitor 3]. Create a feature and strategy comparison matrix. Identify 3 critical 'gaps' in their offerings that my startup can use to steal market share.
proTip: Don't just compete on features; look for gaps in customer service, pricing models, or community building.

title: The Pitch Deck Architect
useCase: Structuring a 10-slide deck to raise capital.
promptText: I need to build a pitch deck for my [Industry] startup to raise a [Seed / Series A] round. Give me a slide-by-slide outline for a 10-slide deck. For each slide, tell me the main headline I should use, the key data points to include, and the emotional takeaway the investor should have.
proTip: Keep the 'Problem' slide incredibly relatable. If the investor doesn't feel the pain of the problem, they won't care about the solution.

title: The 'Mom Test' Interviewer
useCase: Writing unbiased questions to validate a product idea.
promptText: I want to validate my idea for a [Product Idea] targeting [Target Audience]. Write 5 user interview questions following the principles of 'The Mom Test'. The questions must focus on the user's past behavior and current problems, NOT asking them if they think my idea is good.
proTip: Never ask 'Would you buy this?' People will lie to spare your feelings. Ask 'How much do you currently spend trying to solve this?'

title: The Go-To-Market (GTM) Strategist
useCase: Figuring out how to acquire your first 100 paying users.
promptText: I am launching a B2B SaaS for [Target Audience]. The price point is [Price]. Outline a scrappy, zero-budget Go-To-Market strategy to get my first 100 paying customers. Give me 3 highly specific acquisition channels and the exact messaging I should use in those channels.
proTip: In the early days, do things that don't scale. Sending highly personalized cold DMs usually beats running cheap ads.

title: The Pricing Model Brainstormer
useCase: Deciding how to charge for your product.
promptText: My product helps [Target Audience] to [Core Benefit]. Suggest 3 different pricing models (e.g., Freemium, Usage-Based, Flat Tiered). Detail the pros and cons of each for my specific business, and recommend which one I should start with.
proTip: Value-based pricing is almost always better than cost-plus pricing. Charge based on the money or time you save the user.

title: The Product Hunt Launch Plan
useCase: Getting top 3 on Product Hunt launch day.
promptText: I am launching my startup on Product Hunt on [Launch Date]. Create a step-by-step checklist of what I need to do 1 week before launch, the day of the launch, and the day after. Write the copy for the 'Maker's Comment' I should post when it goes live.
proTip: The Maker's Comment should be vulnerable. Talk about *why* you built it and the struggles you faced, not just the features.

title: The Cold Email to Investors
useCase: Writing a cold outreach email to a VC or Angel.
promptText: Write a 4-sentence cold email to a VC who specializes in [VC Niche]. I am raising a [Round Size] round for my startup, [Startup Name]. Our traction so far is [Insert Metric, e.g., $10k MRR, 5000 waitlist]. The goal of the email is to get a 15-minute intro call.
proTip: Investors skim. Use bullet points for traction metrics and bold the most impressive numbers.

title: The Startup Naming Wizard
useCase: Brainstorming modern, brandable startup names.
promptText: I am building a company that does [Company Description] for [Target Audience]. Generate 15 modern startup names. Give me 5 names that are completely made-up words (like Google/Figma), 5 that combine two words (like Facebook/Snapchat), and 5 that use real words with a 'tech' twist.
proTip: Once you pick a name, check trademark databases before buying the domain!

title: The Unit Economics Calculator
useCase: Figuring out if your business model is actually profitable.
promptText: Act as a CFO. I sell a [Product Type] for [Price]. My Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) is roughly [CAC Amount]. My churn rate is [Churn Rate %]. Explain how to calculate my Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) and tell me if my LTV:CAC ratio is healthy for a venture-backed startup.
proTip: A healthy SaaS LTV:CAC ratio is generally considered to be 3:1 or higher.

title: The Elevator Pitch Crafter
useCase: Explaining what you do in under 30 seconds.
promptText: My startup helps [Audience] solve [Problem] by [Solution]. Write 3 versions of an elevator pitch. One version for a tech-savvy investor, one version for a potential customer, and one '5-year-old' version I can use at a dinner party.
proTip: Avoid 'We are the Uber for X'. Focus purely on the problem you solve.

title: The Feature Prioritization Matrix (RICE)
useCase: Deciding what to build next when everything feels urgent.
promptText: I have 3 features I want to build: 1. [Feature 1], 2. [Feature 2], 3. [Feature 3]. Walk me through how to score these using the RICE framework (Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort) so my engineering team knows what to tackle first.
proTip: Effort is usually the dealbreaker. A low-impact feature with massive effort should be killed immediately.

title: The Co-Founder Agreement Outliner
useCase: Structuring equity and vesting before things get messy.
promptText: I am bringing on a technical co-founder. I will handle [My Roles] and they will handle [Their Roles]. Suggest a standard equity split and explain how a '4-year vesting schedule with a 1-year cliff' works in plain English so we can put it in our agreement.
proTip: Never do a 50/50 split without vesting. If someone leaves in month 2, they shouldn't own half the company forever.

title: The B2B Sales Script
useCase: Writing a script for cold calling or product demos.
promptText: I am selling [B2B Software] to [Target Persona, e.g., VP of HR]. Write a 2-minute discovery call script. Include the opening hook, 3 deep 'pain-discovery' questions I should ask them, and a smooth transition to booking a full product demo.
proTip: The best salespeople listen 80% of the time and talk 20%. Ensure your questions are open-ended.

title: The Churn Reduction Strategist
useCase: Stopping users from canceling their subscriptions.
promptText: My SaaS app currently has a [Number]% monthly churn rate. Users typically cancel because [Reason for Canceling]. Give me 3 immediate product changes and 3 automated email campaigns I can implement to win them back or prevent the cancellation in the first place.
proTip: Implement an 'Exit Survey' immediately. You can't fix churn if you don't have data on exactly why they are leaving.

title: The Mission & Vision Statement
useCase: Defining the core culture and goal of your company.
promptText: My company is called [Company Name] and we build [Product]. Our ultimate goal in 10 years is to [Long-term Goal]. Draft a 1-sentence Mission Statement (what we do right now) and a 1-sentence Vision Statement (the future we are trying to create). Make them inspiring, not corporate jargon.
proTip: A great vision statement acts as a filter for hiring. If a candidate doesn't align with the vision, don't hire them.

title: The Value Proposition Canvas
useCase: Mapping exactly how your product creates customer joy.
promptText: I am targeting [Customer Persona]. Fill out a Value Proposition Canvas for this customer. List 3 'Customer Jobs' they are trying to do, 3 'Pains' they experience, and 3 'Gains' they want. Then, list how my product, [Product Name], provides Pain Relievers and Gain Creators.
proTip: Focus on emotional pains, not just functional ones. (e.g., 'Looking bad in front of my boss' is a huge emotional pain).

title: The Pivot Brainstormer
useCase: Finding a new direction when growth stalls.
promptText: We built a [Describe Current Product], but growth is completely flat. Our users actually only use the [Specific Feature] feature, and ignore everything else. Give me 3 ideas for how we could 'pivot' the company to focus entirely on that one feature. What would the new business model look like?
proTip: Some of the biggest companies (like Slack and Instagram) started as entirely different products before pivoting to their most popular feature.

title: The Freemium vs. Free Trial Decider
useCase: Choosing the best way to let users test your app.
promptText: I have a SaaS app that does [App Function]. It costs me [Cost, e.g., $0.05] every time a user runs a query. Should I offer a 14-day Free Trial or a permanent Freemium tier? Explain the psychology behind both and recommend the best path for my specific costs.
proTip: If your marginal cost per user is high (like AI text generation), Freemium can bankrupt you quickly. Go with a Trial.

title: The Dockerfile Generator
useCase: Containerizing an application efficiently.
promptText: Write a highly optimized, multi-stage Dockerfile for a [Language/Framework, e.g., Node.js, Python FastAPI] application. The app runs on port [Port Number]. Ensure the final image is as small as possible and runs as a non-root user for security.
proTip: Multi-stage builds are crucial for compiled languages (like Go or Rust) to keep the final production image tiny.

title: The CI/CD Pipeline Builder
useCase: Automating testing and deployment with GitHub Actions.
promptText: Generate a GitHub Actions workflow YAML file for a [Language] project. It should trigger on pushes to the 'main' branch. The pipeline needs to run tests, build a Docker image, and push the image to [Container Registry, e.g., AWS ECR, Docker Hub]. Include caching to speed up the build.
proTip: Never hardcode secrets in your YAML. Always ask the AI to use `${{ secrets.MY_SECRET }}`.

title: The Terraform Scripter
useCase: Defining Infrastructure as Code (IaC) for cloud providers.
promptText: Write a Terraform script (main.tf) to provision an [Cloud Provider, e.g., AWS] infrastructure. I need an EC2 instance running Ubuntu, a security group that allows SSH (port 22) and HTTP (port 80), and an attached RDS PostgreSQL database. Use best practices for variable management.
proTip: Always ask the AI to split the code into `main.tf`, `variables.tf`, and `outputs.tf` for better maintainability.

title: The AWS Architecture Planner
useCase: Designing scalable, highly-available cloud systems.
promptText: I am designing a backend architecture for a highly scalable [App Type, e.g., e-commerce site, video streaming app] using AWS. The traffic will be spiky. Outline the services I should use for Compute, Database, Storage, and Caching. Explain how traffic flows from the user to the database.
proTip: Ask the AI to design for 'High Availability' (Multi-AZ) and 'Fault Tolerance'.

title: The Bash Automation Script
useCase: Writing Linux shell scripts for server maintenance.
promptText: Write a robust bash script that will automatically [Task, e.g., backup a PostgreSQL database, tar the file, and upload it to an S3 bucket]. The script should include error handling, logging, and exit immediately if any command fails (set -e).
proTip: Add a cron expression request to the prompt so you know exactly how to schedule the script to run daily.

title: The Kubernetes Manifest Writer
useCase: Deploying apps to a K8s cluster without fighting YAML.
promptText: Generate Kubernetes YAML manifests for a [App Name] deployment. I need a Deployment with 3 replicas, a Service of type [Service Type, e.g., ClusterIP, LoadBalancer], and an Ingress rule mapping to [Domain Name]. Include resource limits (CPU/Memory) for the containers.
proTip: Resource limits are essential. Without them, a memory leak in one pod can crash your entire Kubernetes node.

title: The IAM Policy Architect
useCase: Generating secure, least-privilege cloud permissions.
promptText: Write an AWS IAM JSON policy that follows the principle of least privilege. The user/role only needs permission to [Specific Action, e.g., read and write to a specific S3 bucket named 'my-app-assets', and trigger a specific Lambda function]. Deny all other access.
proTip: Never use `"Action": "s3:*"` in production. Always narrow it down to exactly `GetObject` and `PutObject`.

title: The Cloud Cost Optimizer
useCase: Finding ways to slash your AWS/GCP/Azure bill.
promptText: My AWS bill is getting too high. We heavily use [List Heavy Services, e.g., EC2, RDS, NAT Gateways]. Give me 5 advanced strategies to optimize our cloud costs without sacrificing performance or uptime. Specifically mention Reserved Instances and Spot Instances if applicable.
proTip: NAT Gateways are notorious for hidden data transfer costs. Ask the AI for alternatives like VPC Endpoints.

title: The Nginx Config Generator
useCase: Setting up reverse proxies and SSL.
promptText: Generate a production-ready Nginx configuration file (`nginx.conf`). It needs to act as a reverse proxy, listening on port 80 and 443, redirecting HTTP to HTTPS, and forwarding traffic to a backend app running on `localhost:[Port]`. Include basic security headers.
proTip: Ask the AI to include Let's Encrypt (Certbot) snippets if you are setting this up on a fresh VPS.

title: The Prometheus Alert Rules
useCase: Setting up monitoring alerts before things crash.
promptText: I am using Prometheus and Alertmanager. Write the YAML alert rules for a [Service Type, e.g., Node Exporter, PostgreSQL]. Create a critical alert if CPU usage goes over 85% for 5 minutes, and a warning alert if disk space drops below 15%.
proTip: Alert fatigue is real. Make sure you set a reasonable `for:` duration so random 10-second spikes don't wake you up at 3 AM.

title: The Incident Post-Mortem
useCase: Writing a blameless Root Cause Analysis (RCA) after downtime.
promptText: We just had a major production incident where [Describe Outage, e.g., the database ran out of connections due to a bad code push]. Write a formal, blameless Post-Mortem document. Include sections for: Lead-up, Fault, Impact, Root Cause (using the 5 Whys), and Action Items to prevent recurrence.
proTip: Blameless RCAs focus on systemic failures. Instead of 'Dev pushed bad code', write 'CI/CD pipeline lacked testing for max connections'.

title: The Server Hardening Checklist
useCase: Securing a fresh Linux VPS against attacks.
promptText: I just provisioned a fresh [OS, e.g., Ubuntu 22.04] server on DigitalOcean/AWS. Give me a step-by-step bash script or checklist to harden the server. Include setting up a firewall (UFW), disabling root SSH login, changing the default SSH port, and setting up Fail2Ban.
proTip: Always verify your new SSH port works in a separate terminal before closing your current root session, or you'll lock yourself out!

title: The Log Analysis Regex
useCase: Parsing massive access logs to find errors or hackers.
promptText: I have a massive [Server Type, e.g., Nginx, Apache] access log. I need a grep/awk command or a Regex pattern to parse this log and extract only the [Data Needed, e.g., IP addresses that received a 500 Internal Server Error]. Provide the command and explain how it filters the text.
proTip: You can also ask the AI to sort the output and `uniq -c` to count the most frequent offending IP addresses.

title: The Serverless Function Outliner
useCase: Writing scalable AWS Lambda functions.
promptText: Write the code for an AWS Lambda function in [Language, e.g., Python, Node.js]. The function is triggered by an S3 event when a [File Type] is uploaded. It needs to [Action, e.g., resize the image, parse the CSV] and save the result to a DynamoDB table. Include the necessary IAM permissions required.
proTip: Lambda timeouts default to 3 seconds. Ask the AI what timeout and memory size you should configure for your specific task.

title: The Ansible Playbook Creator
useCase: Automating server configuration management.
promptText: Write an Ansible playbook in YAML. It needs to target the `[Host Group]` group. The playbook should update apt packages, install [Software List, e.g., Docker, Git, htop], and start the Docker service. Ensure the tasks are idempotent.
proTip: Idempotency is the golden rule of Ansible. Running the playbook 10 times should result in the exact same state as running it once.

title: The Network CIDR Planner
useCase: Designing an AWS VPC without IP collisions.
promptText: I am creating a new AWS VPC. I need a base CIDR block of [CIDR, e.g., 10.0.0.0/16]. Divide this into 2 Public Subnets and 2 Private Subnets across two Availability Zones. Tell me the exact CIDR ranges for each subnet and how many usable IPs they contain.
proTip: Leave gaps in your IP planning! Ask the AI to reserve space for future subnets (like database-specific subnets).

title: The Load Balancing Strategist
useCase: Deciding how to route traffic to your servers.
promptText: I am setting up a load balancer for my [App Type] application. Should I use a Layer 4 (Network/TCP) load balancer or a Layer 7 (Application/HTTP) load balancer? Explain the difference, the pros/cons of each, and recommend the best strategy for sticky sessions.
proTip: If you need to route traffic based on the URL path (e.g., `/api` goes to one server, `/blog` to another), you MUST use Layer 7.

title: The Database Migration Script
useCase: Safely altering database schemas in production.
promptText: I need to write a zero-downtime database migration for a [Database Type, e.g., PostgreSQL] database. I need to add a new column called `[Column Name]` to the `[Table Name]` table, backfill it with a default value of `[Value]`, and then make it NOT NULL. Provide the SQL commands.
proTip: Adding a default value to a massive table can lock the table and cause downtime. Ask the AI for the 'concurrent' or safe approach.

title: The Helm Chart Structurer
useCase: Packaging Kubernetes applications.
promptText: Explain the directory structure of a standard Helm Chart for a [App Type] application. Provide a boilerplate `values.yaml` file that includes configurable variables for image repository, image tag, replica count, and ingress hostnames.
proTip: Helm templates can get messy. Keep your `values.yaml` clean and well-commented so other developers know what they can override.

title: The Command Line Troubleshooter
useCase: Figuring out why a Linux server is failing.
promptText: My Linux server is currently [Symptom, e.g., running at 100% CPU, running out of disk space, dropping network packets]. Give me the top 5 bash commands I should run immediately to diagnose the root cause, and explain exactly what I should be looking for in the output.
proTip: Commands like `htop`, `df -h`, and `netstat -tulpn` are lifesavers. Ask the AI how to interpret the specific columns they output.

title: The Immersive Roleplayer
useCase: Practicing real-life conversations before traveling.
promptText: Act as a native [Target Language] speaker who works as a [Role, e.g., waiter, train ticket agent] in [City/Country]. I am a tourist trying to [Goal, e.g., order a traditional meal, find my platform]. Let's roleplay. Speak only in [Target Language]. Wait for my response before replying. Correct my mistakes in English at the end of each reply.
proTip: Tell the AI to keep its responses at a specific proficiency level (e.g., A2 Beginner or B2 Intermediate) so it doesn't overwhelm you.

title: The Grammar Demystifier
useCase: Understanding confusing grammar rules without a textbook.
promptText: I am learning [Target Language]. I am constantly confused by the difference between [Grammar Rule 1, e.g., Por] and [Grammar Rule 2, e.g., Para]. Explain the difference in plain English, provide 3 simple examples for each, and then give me a 5-question quiz to test my understanding.
proTip: Don't just read the explanation—actually answer the quiz! Active recall is the fastest way to cement grammar rules.

title: The Local Slang Translator
useCase: Sounding like a local, not a textbook robot.
promptText: I am traveling to [Specific City/Region, e.g., Buenos Aires, Argentina]. Textbooks teach me standard [Language, e.g., Spanish], but I want to sound like a local. Give me 10 common slang words or idioms specific to this exact region, what they literally mean, and how to use them in a casual sentence.
proTip: Regional dialects matter. Spanish in Madrid is wildly different from Spanish in Mexico City. Always specify the exact city.

title: The Flashcard Generator
useCase: Building Anki or Quizlet decks rapidly.
promptText: I am learning [Target Language]. Generate a table of 20 high-frequency vocabulary words related to [Topic, e.g., navigating an airport, medical emergencies]. Column 1: The word in [Target Language]. Column 2: The English translation. Column 3: A practical example sentence in [Target Language].
proTip: You can export this table directly as a CSV and import it into Anki or Quizlet in seconds.

title: The Tone & Politeness Checker
useCase: Avoiding accidental rudeness in formal cultures.
promptText: I need to send an email to a [Recipient, e.g., potential boss, landlord] in [Target Language]. I drafted this: [Insert Draft]. Correct my grammar, but more importantly, adjust the 'politeness level' (formality) to perfectly match the cultural expectations of [Target Country]. Explain what you changed.
proTip: Languages like Japanese and Korean have strict formality hierarchies. Always specify who you are talking to.

title: The Journal Corrector
useCase: Getting instant feedback on your daily writing practice.
promptText: I wrote a short diary entry in [Target Language] to practice my writing. Here it is: [Insert Text]. First, point out my grammatical errors and unnatural phrasing. Then, rewrite the entire entry exactly how a native speaker would actually say it.
proTip: Compare your original text side-by-side with the AI's rewrite. Note the different prepositions and verb choices.

title: The False Friend Finder
useCase: Avoiding embarrassing translation mistakes.
promptText: I am a native English speaker learning [Target Language]. Provide a list of the 10 most dangerous 'false friends' (cognates that look like English words but mean something completely different). Explain the real meaning and how to actually say the English word I was thinking of.
proTip: For example, 'Embarazada' in Spanish means pregnant, not embarrassed! This prompt saves you from awkward moments.

title: The Graded Reader Storyteller
useCase: Practicing reading comprehension at your exact level.
promptText: Write a short, engaging fiction story (about 300 words) in [Target Language] about [Topic, e.g., a detective solving a mystery]. Keep the vocabulary and grammar strictly at a [CEFR Level, e.g., A2, B1] proficiency level. At the end, ask me 3 reading comprehension questions in English.
proTip: If a word is too hard, ask the AI to generate a glossary of the top 10 hardest words before the story begins.

title: The Phonetic Pronunciation Guide
useCase: Nailing difficult sounds and accents.
promptText: I am struggling to pronounce the [Specific Sound, e.g., rolled 'R' in Spanish, French 'U']. Explain the exact physical tongue and lip placement required to make this sound. Give me 5 phonetic warm-up exercises to practice.
proTip: Use this in combination with a text-to-speech tool to hear the sound while you practice the physical mouth movements.

title: The Pop Culture Translator
useCase: Learning through music, movies, and TV.
promptText: Analyze the lyrics to the song [Song Name] by [Artist] in [Target Language]. Provide the original lyrics, the direct English translation, and a breakdown of any slang, cultural references, or poetic metaphors used in the song.
proTip: Listening to music with a deep understanding of the lyrics is one of the best passive immersion techniques.

title: The Idiom Decoder
useCase: Understanding phrases that make zero sense literally.
promptText: In English, we say [English Idiom, e.g., 'It's raining cats and dogs' or 'Break a leg']. What is the exact equivalent idiom in [Target Language]? Provide the literal translation of their idiom and an example of how to use it in conversation.
proTip: Translating idioms literally usually results in nonsense. Always ask for the *cultural equivalent*.

title: The Debate Partner
useCase: Practicing advanced, argumentative vocabulary.
promptText: I want to practice my advanced [Target Language]. Let's debate the topic: [Debate Topic, e.g., Is remote work better than office work?]. You take the opposing side. Speak at a [CEFR Level, e.g., C1] level. Make a strong argument and wait for my rebuttal.
proTip: This forces you to learn transition words like 'Furthermore', 'However', and 'On the contrary' in your target language.

title: The Menu Navigator
useCase: Ordering food confidently without pointing at pictures.
promptText: I am going to a traditional restaurant in [Country/Region]. List 10 authentic local dishes I will likely see on the menu. Explain what they are in English, and provide the phonetic pronunciation for how to order them politely in [Target Language].
proTip: Ask the AI to include phrases for dietary restrictions (e.g., 'Does this have peanuts?', 'I am vegetarian').

title: The Etiquette & Taboo Guide
useCase: Avoiding cultural faux pas while traveling.
promptText: I am traveling to [Country] for the first time. Beyond just the language, what are 5 strict cultural do's and don'ts? Specifically, tell me about greeting etiquette, tipping culture, and one common gesture tourists make that is actually offensive there.
proTip: Language is only half the battle; cultural context is the other half. Knowing how to bow or shake hands changes everything.

title: The Mnemonic Creator
useCase: Memorizing stubborn vocabulary words that won't stick.
promptText: I am trying to memorize the [Target Language] word '[Target Word]', which means '[English Meaning]'. Create 3 funny, bizarre, or highly visual mnemonic memory hooks to help me permanently remember this word.
proTip: The weirder the mental image, the more likely your brain is to remember it. Don't be afraid to ask for 'ridiculous' mnemonics.

title: The Transition Word Bank
useCase: Sounding fluent by connecting your sentences smoothly.
promptText: My [Target Language] sounds very choppy. I just string simple sentences together. Give me a categorized list of 15 essential 'transition words' (e.g., however, therefore, suddenly, by the way) with example sentences showing how to use them to flow better.
proTip: Transition words are the secret to moving from an A2 (Beginner) to a B1 (Intermediate) speaking level.

title: The Test Prep Examiner (JLPT, DELE, etc.)
useCase: Simulating official language proficiency exams.
promptText: I am studying for the [Exam Name, e.g., JLPT N3, DELE B2, DELF]. Generate a mock 'Reading Comprehension' section specifically tailored to this exact exam level. Provide a short text, followed by 3 multiple-choice questions. Do not give me the answers until I guess.
proTip: Specify the exam name. AI knows the exact formatting and vocabulary lists for major global language exams.

title: The Suffix/Prefix Expander
useCase: Multiplying your vocabulary by understanding word roots.
promptText: In [Target Language], how do prefixes and suffixes work? Take the root word for '[Root Word, e.g., Write, Speak]' and show me how adding different prefixes or suffixes creates 5-10 completely new words. Explain the pattern.
proTip: Learning patterns is faster than memorizing individual words. Once you know how '-tion' translates, you unlock hundreds of words.

title: The Tense Time-Traveler
useCase: Mastering past, present, and future conjugations.
promptText: I struggle with verb conjugations in [Target Language]. Give me a simple paragraph written entirely in the Present Tense about a daily routine. Then, rewrite that exact same paragraph in the [Target Tense, e.g., Preterite Past, Future Perfect]. Bold the verbs that changed.
proTip: Seeing the exact same story shift timelines helps your brain isolate exactly how the verbs mutate.

title: The Language Immersion Planner
useCase: Creating a daily routine to surround yourself with the language.
promptText: I want to learn [Target Language] but I live in [Your Country] and can't travel. Create a daily 'At-Home Immersion' routine that requires exactly [Minutes] minutes a day. Include passive methods (like podcasts/music) and active methods. Suggest specific media or apps.
proTip: Change your phone and laptop OS language to your target language for guaranteed daily passive exposure.

title: The Debt Destroyer (Avalanche vs Snowball)
useCase: Creating a mathematical and psychological plan to get out of debt.
promptText: I have [Number] debts. Debt 1: [Amount] at [APR]%. Debt 2: [Amount] at [APR]%. Debt 3: [Amount] at [APR]%. I have an extra [Monthly Budget] per month to put towards debt. Compare the 'Debt Snowball' and 'Debt Avalanche' methods for my specific numbers. Which one saves me more money, and which one gets me a win faster?
proTip: The Avalanche method always saves the most money (math), but the Snowball method builds the most momentum (psychology).

title: The ELI5 Investing Explainer
useCase: Understanding Wall Street jargon without a finance degree.
promptText: Explain the difference between [Financial Concept A, e.g., an ETF] and [Financial Concept B, e.g., a Mutual Fund] like I am a 5-year-old. Use a simple, everyday analogy (like buying groceries or pizza) to explain the fees, the risks, and why someone would choose one over the other.
proTip: Use this prompt to decode anything: Roth IRA vs. Traditional IRA, Stocks vs. Bonds, or Crypto vs. Fiat.

title: The 50/30/20 Budget Architect
useCase: Structuring your paycheck instantly based on standard rules.
promptText: My monthly take-home pay (after taxes) is [Income Amount]. Create a strict 50/30/20 budget for me. Calculate the exact dollar amounts for 'Needs' (50%), 'Wants' (30%), and 'Savings/Investing' (20%). Give me 3 examples of expenses that fit into each category.
proTip: If you live in a high-cost-of-living city, ask the AI to adjust the ratio to 60/20/20 to account for higher rent.

title: The Expense Audit Interrogator
useCase: Finding the 'leaks' in your monthly spending.
promptText: Act as a strict financial advisor. I spend roughly [Amount] on groceries, [Amount] on dining out/delivery, and [Amount] on subscriptions every month. Tell me the harsh truth about my spending. Ask me 3 challenging questions to help me cut the fat from this budget without feeling miserable.
proTip: People usually underestimate their dining out budget by 30%. Pull your actual bank statements before inputting these numbers.

title: The Emergency Fund Calculator
useCase: Figuring out exactly how much cash you need to be safe.
promptText: My absolute bare-minimum survival expenses (rent, groceries, basic utilities) are [Amount] per month. I work as a [Your Profession/Industry]. Based on the current job market and my industry, should my emergency fund be 3, 6, or 12 months? Calculate the exact goal amount and give me a monthly saving plan to hit it in [Timeframe].
proTip: Freelancers and gig workers usually need a 6-12 month fund, while tenured public workers might only need 3 months.

title: The Compound Interest Time-Traveler
useCase: Visualizing how small investments turn into millions.
promptText: I am [Age] years old. I have [Current Savings] invested right now. If I invest [Monthly Contribution] every single month into an S&P 500 index fund (assuming a 7% average annual return adjusted for inflation), exactly how much money will I have when I am 65? How much of that total is just pure compound interest?
proTip: Ask the AI to show you how much you'd lose if you wait just 5 years to start doing this. The 'Cost of Waiting' is staggering.

title: The Salary Negotiation Script
useCase: Getting paid what you are worth without sounding arrogant.
promptText: I have been offered a job as a [Job Title]. They offered [Offer Amount], but the market rate is closer to [Target Amount]. Write a professional, collaborative email to the recruiter negotiating for [Target Amount]. Focus the argument on my unique value: [Your Unique Skill/Experience].
proTip: Never anchor on your personal expenses (e.g., 'I need more for rent'). Always anchor on market data and the value you bring.

title: The Bill Negotiation Script
useCase: Lowering your internet, cable, or insurance bills over the phone.
promptText: I need to call my [Company Type, e.g., Internet Provider, Car Insurance] to lower my monthly bill, which is currently [Current Bill Amount]. Write a step-by-step phone script. Include exactly what to say to the first rep, how to ask for the Retention Department, and what competitor threat I should use.
proTip: The 'Retention Department' (or cancellations) is the only department with the actual power to lower your bill.

title: The Credit Score Optimizer
useCase: Understanding the exact levers that dictate your FICO score.
promptText: My credit score recently dropped, or I want to improve it. Explain the 5 main factors that make up a FICO credit score (Payment History, Utilization, Age, Mix, New Credit) and give me one highly actionable tactic to immediately improve my 'Credit Utilization Ratio' without paying off debt.
proTip: A quick hack to lower utilization is asking your credit card company for a 'Credit Limit Increase' while keeping your spending the same.

title: The Rent vs. Buy Math Engine
useCase: Making the biggest financial decision of your life with math, not emotion.
promptText: I am debating renting vs. buying a home. Rent for a place I like is [Rent Amount]/month. A similar home costs [Home Price] with a [Interest Rate]% mortgage rate. Factor in taxes, maintenance (1% rule), insurance, and the opportunity cost of investing my down payment. Give me a 10-year financial breakdown of which is actually cheaper.
proTip: Most people forget the 'Opportunity Cost'. If you invest a $50k down payment in the stock market instead of a house, it grows significantly.

title: The Side Hustle Brainstormer
useCase: Finding realistic ways to increase your income based on your skills.
promptText: I want to start a side hustle to make an extra [Target Amount] a month. My day job is [Current Job], my core skills are [List 3 Skills], and I have [Number of Hours] hours a week to dedicate to this. Give me 5 realistic, low-upfront-cost side hustle ideas. Rank them by how fast they can generate the first $100.
proTip: Avoid passive income pipe-dreams. Ask the AI for 'active' freelancing or service-based hustles for the fastest cash flow.

title: The Financial Milestone Roadmap
useCase: Breaking down a massive financial goal into daily targets.
promptText: I want to save [Target Amount] for a [Goal, e.g., house down payment, wedding] in exactly [Number of Months] months. Break this massive number down. How much do I need to save per month, per week, and per day? Suggest 3 daily habits I can cut to hit this daily target.
proTip: Seeing a $20,000 goal as just '$18 a day' makes it psychologically much easier to achieve.

title: The 'FIRE' Number Calculator
useCase: Calculating exactly how much you need to retire early.
promptText: I am interested in the FIRE movement (Financial Independence, Retire Early). My estimated annual expenses in retirement will be [Annual Expense Amount]. Explain the '4% Rule' (Trinity Study) and calculate my exact 'FIRE Number'. Then, tell me how a 3.5% safe withdrawal rate changes that target.
proTip: The basic math is just your annual expenses multiplied by 25. The hard part is getting there.

title: The Psychology of Spending
useCase: Identifying emotional triggers that ruin your budget.
promptText: I often impulse-buy things online late at night or when I am stressed. Act as a financial therapist. Explain the dopamine loop of impulse shopping and give me 3 psychological friction tactics (e.g., the 24-hour rule) I can implement to stop myself from checking out.
proTip: Ask the AI to draft a 'Pre-Purchase Checklist' you can stick on your monitor before buying anything over $50.

title: The Subscription Purge Audit
useCase: Finding hidden monthly costs.
promptText: I have the following recurring monthly subscriptions: [List Subscriptions and Prices]. Categorize them into 'High Value' and 'Low Value'. Calculate how much I am spending per year on these. If I cancel the bottom 3 and invest that money at 7% for 10 years, how much will I have?
proTip: People look at subscriptions as '$10 a month', but you should look at them as '$120 a year'. The annual framing changes everything.

title: The Tax Basics Translator
useCase: Understanding marginal tax brackets.
promptText: Explain how 'Marginal Tax Brackets' work using a simple analogy (like filling up buckets of water). If I get a raise that pushes me into a higher tax bracket, will my entire income be taxed at that higher rate? Debunk this common myth.
proTip: Never decline a raise because you think taxes will make you earn less. That is mathematically impossible in a marginal system.

title: The Freelance Tax Prep
useCase: Preparing for self-employment taxes without panic.
promptText: I just started freelancing/gig work as a [Job Type] and I expect to make [Estimated Income] this year. I live in [State/Country]. Explain how 'Self-Employment Tax' works, why I need to pay quarterly estimated taxes, and exactly what percentage of every paycheck I should hide in a separate savings account.
proTip: A common rule of thumb is hiding 30% of every freelance check for taxes, but ask the AI for specifics based on your state.

title: The Asset Allocation Architect
useCase: Understanding how to balance risk in an investment portfolio.
promptText: I am [Age] years old. I have a [Risk Tolerance, e.g., conservative, aggressive] risk tolerance. Explain the concept of 'Asset Allocation' (Stocks vs. Bonds). What is a standard portfolio breakdown for someone my age? Mention the '110 minus your age' rule and explain why it exists.
proTip: This is for educational purposes only. Always consult a real fiduciary before making massive portfolio changes.

title: The Inflation & Purchasing Power Guide
useCase: Understanding why leaving cash in a checking account is losing money.
promptText: I have [Amount] sitting in a regular checking account earning 0% interest. Assuming an average annual inflation rate of 3%, calculate how much 'purchasing power' this money will lose in 5 years and 10 years. Explain the concept of a High-Yield Savings Account (HYSA) as a defense.
proTip: Inflation is the invisible tax. Ask the AI to compare your checking account against a 4.5% HYSA over 5 years.

title: The Weekly Money Routine
useCase: Creating a low-stress habit for managing wealth.
promptText: I get anxious looking at my bank account. Create a low-stress, 15-minute 'Financial Friday' routine for me. What are the 3 exact things I should check, update, or pay every single week to stay in control of my money without obsessing over it daily?
proTip: Consistency beats intensity. A 15-minute weekly check-in is infinitely better than a 4-hour stressful budget overhaul once a year.
